standard.title: Collaborate in transaction, negotiation and problem-solving
standard.description: collaborate in activities that involve the language of transaction, negotiation and problem-solving to plan projects and events
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can participate in planning and negotiating with others, expressing preferences and ideas (AC9LS6C02). They negotiate preferences and manage decisions. They have not yet engaged in transactional or directional language, or problem-solving that addresses genuine issues for real audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students collaborate in activities involving transaction, negotiation and problem-solving — conducting transactions, giving directions, contributing perspectives on shared issues, and producing collaborative outputs for the school community.

nodes.label: Transactional and directional language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use transactional language for purchases and services, and directional language for navigation — in simulated and real contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Conduct a transaction using at least three target language exchanges including a price or option and a decision; give or follow at least two directional instructions.
nodes.typical_width: Role-play transactions across purchase and service contexts; give and follow multi-step directions using maps or spatial references; complete tasks requiring requesting, confirming and following directions to real or virtual locations.
wider: Conduct a full transaction — enquiry, negotiation, decision — in an unrehearsed scenario with an open outcome
Give directions to a genuinely unfamiliar destination using only the target language — including landmarks, distances and transport options
nodes.hinge_reason: Transactional and directional language are the foundational practical tasks of the problem-solving dimension. Students who cannot manage basic transactions and directions cannot engage with the more complex collaborative problem-solving and project work in node 2.

response_modes.reason: Transaction and direction language needs practice across varied contexts — different transaction types, locations and interlocutor conditions — before it transfers to unrehearsed situations.

success_criteria: Conducts a transaction using at least three target language exchanges including a price or option and a decision
Gives or follows at least two directional instructions using appropriate spatial language

nodes.label: Collaborative problem-solving and shared outputs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaborate in problem-solving activities and produce shared outputs — including digital products and community resources — using negotiation, task delegation and reflection.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute at least one perspective, negotiate at least one decision and reflect on at least one aspect of the process in a collaborative problem-solving task.
nodes.typical_width: Work in teams to solve shared problems; contribute and listen to multiple perspectives; produce collaborative outputs (bilingual resources, community materials, digital products); divide and delegate tasks; reflect on collaborative process and outcomes.
wider: Lead a collaborative project from problem identification to shared output — managing task delegation, progress checking and presentation
Produce a genuine community resource in the target language for real school use — evaluate the product's effectiveness for its intended audience

response_modes.reason: Collaborative problem-solving integrates transactional language (N1) with negotiation, perspective-sharing and project management — all applied in a real production task with genuine stakes.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Producing genuine community resources for real audiences is where collaborative language use becomes genuinely purposeful — students at this level can produce target language content that serves their actual school community.
success_criteria: Contributes at least one perspective and negotiates at least one decision in a collaborative task
Contributes to a shared output that could serve a real communicative purpose
